second_order: figuring out the April Fools switch
theme_note: These exchanges hold together because people encounter, explain, confirm, or date the room's own April Fools changes. What varies is whether the switch is Forsen, the TSM banner, or the whole subreddit restyling, and whether a person is confused, explaining, or fixing it.

second_order: following and cheering C9's new memer
theme_note: These passages respond to the Forsen announcement by placing him among C9's memers, deciding to watch him, and cheering him. The practice varies from characterising the signing to taking up fandom.
regrouped_from: Split from 'figuring out the April Fools switch' on review because these passages take up the announced streamer rather than work out the joke.

second_order: getting a C9 logo onto the canvas
theme_note: These codes enact the shared effort to make C9 visible: calling for a logo, retrying after failure, locating work, joining, recruiting, doing the long build, and marking its completion. What varies is who drives the attempt and whether the moment is mobilisation, labour, or thanks.

second_order: working out how the logo should look
theme_note: These passages turn an intended logo into pixel instructions by asking for a shape, proposing a blueprint, setting colour and white-space rules, joining a rainbow, and proposing lettering. The details vary from first sketch to later repair and colour choices.
regrouped_from: Split from 'getting a C9 logo onto the canvas' because these codes decide the shared design rather than recruit or perform the build.

second_order: answering for what the C9 logo covered
theme_note: One exchange holds these together: a visitor says a long-built sign was erased, a C9 participant recognises and apologises, the opener regrets what was covered, and the visitor accepts the crowd outcome. The variation is accusation, accountability, and acceptance.

These codes contest whether C9 participants should replace, invade, or expand into neighbours' pixels. Calls to take space are answered by refusals, moral criticism, warnings against retaliation, and reminders that the neighbour helped.
regrouped_from: Pulled together from separate TSM and r/furry exchanges after the grouping review because both are arguments over whether taking a neighbour's worked pixels is acceptable, not merely mentions of different groups.

theme_note: These passages recruit help, welcome it, repair damage, and call defenders when the logo is being overwritten. The variation runs from routine upkeep described as janitor duty to urgent calls during a claimed bot attack.

second_order: working out who was damaging the logos
theme_note: These exchanges attribute damage, challenge the attribution, ask in another group's Discord, narrow responsibility to two people, or identify C9's own conflicting edits. What varies is the proposed culprit—TSM, CLG, a few individuals, C9 builders, saboteurs, or bot accounts—and none becomes an uncontested causal finding.
regrouped_from: Separated from 'keeping the C9 logo alive' on review because these passages investigate and dispute responsibility; repair is not the practice that holds them together.

second_order: keeping peace and helping across the borders
theme_note: These codes manage coexistence with neighbouring art: warning builders off borders, greeting across communities, maintaining a visible line, requesting and carrying an agreement, offering reciprocal help, helping Smite, recalling a treaty, and denying harmful intent. The practice varies between boundary-setting, assistance, and reassurance.
regrouped_from: Narrowed from an initial 'defending territory' group because these codes coordinate limits and reciprocal help across borders rather than defend only C9's logo.

second_order: moving the C9 build to a permanent Place
theme_note: Both passages respond to the ended canvas by carrying C9-building into PlaceTwo or a described permanent version. One reports doing it; the other recruits help and supplies a relative location.

second_order: remembering a failed Discord plan and a fun build
theme_note: This single code belongs with no other practice: it contrasts failed coordination in the Sneaky Discord with satisfaction at helping in the Reddit-led build.

second_order: making one last attempt as r/place ended
theme_note: The surviving call and its answer form one closing exchange: an ambiguous 'our turn' call is followed by a report that the canvas had ended and a top-swirl attempt failed. The sequence is visible; the removed opening body limits what the call meant.
